FIR is registered for the offences under Section 3 & 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 and Sections 506, 504, 34, 498A, 384, 328, 376 of IPC alleging that, accused No.1 is the husband, and accused No.2 & 3 are the parents in law, and they subjected the respondent No.1 to cruelty both mentally and physically, and also accused No.1 had forcible sexual intercourse.
The registration of the FIR is impugned in this petition.

2. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioners submits that the dispute between the parties arises out of marital discord, however, given criminal texture which is evident from the petition filed by accused No.1 for dissolving the marriage with respondent No.1, and respondent No.2 as an after thought to circumvent the said petitioner No.1, has lodged the FIR.
3. Learned HCGP has placed on record the report submitted by the Jurisdictional Police stating that the respondent No.1-victim, is no more.

4. Learned HCGP appearing for respondent No.2-State submits that the allegations made in the FIR discloses the commission of offences alleged against the petitioners - accused herein, and veracity of the allegations requires to be investigated, and at this stage, registration of FIR does not warrant any indulgence.
5. I have examined the submissions made by the learned counsels for the parties.
6. The marriage of respondent No.1 was solemnized with accused No.1 on 13.06.2013.
The petitioner - accused No.1 had filed MC No.4303/2014 on 13.10.2014 for dissolving his marriage with respondent No.1.
Respondent No.1 filed objections to the said petition and in the said petition, there is no allegation of either cruelty or sexual assault by the accused Nos.1 & 2.
Thereafter, the deceased-respondent No.1 filed MC No.685/2017 for restitution of conjugal right and in the said petition there is no allegation of cruelty or sexual assault by either of the accused.

It is only thereafter, the FIR was lodged by respondent No.1 alleging cruelty and sexual assault, which clearly implies that the FIR was lodged with an intention to circumvent the proceedings initiated by accused No.1 for dissolving the marriage with respondent No.1.

In view of the proceedings analysis, I am of the view that the dispute between the parties arises out of marital discord, however, given a criminal texture to wreak vengeance and with revengeful intent.
Hence, continuation of the criminal proceedings will be an abuse of process of law.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER a. Criminal Petition is allowed; b. Impugned FIR in Cr.No.385/2017 registered by the Vijayanagar Police station, is hereby quashed.
